Under fixed HRT and SRT conditions, pilot-scale MPBR frequently exceeded Italian reuse limit for effluent ammonium (NH4-Neff)
During Periods 1 and 2, compliance was experimentally observed for only approximately 3 days (~8% of operating time)
Period 4 exhibited the highest compliance, with the reuse standard met for nearly 60 of the 89 operating days
Between days 70 and 89, measured NH4-Neff concentration increased sharply and reached the highest experimentally observed values
Deterioration resulted from combined effect of increased NLR (from 17.5 ± 4.6 to 26–34 g N d-1, driven by influent NH4 peak) and nitrifying bacteria proliferation competing for ammonium

González-Camejo et al. [71] described operational/environmental factors in microalgae-nitrifying bacteria competition, noting controlling SRT/HRT (inversely proportional to dilution rate) maximizes microalgae performance by minimizing nitrification
